answer: /graph-find dispatches from graph-find.toml to the graph-find skill, which runs graph_find.py with the repository root and prompt. The adapter verifies the canonical Git root, lists cached Git-tracked paths, rejects unsafe or sensitive paths, reads regular strict-UTF-8 files within caps, and builds in-memory GraphRecord and SourceSnapshotV4 objects with byte lengths and SHA-256 identities. The core builds typed tags from those exact bytes, compiles prompt facets, retrieves through exact/sparse/wiki/graph channels, verifies source custody, ranks bounded hits, and emits source-bound spans. The returned JSON contains route, reason, ranked hits, evidence pointers and hashes, source snapshot SHA-256, context bytes, facet coverage, fallback paths, fail_closed, obligation status, remaining budget, score meaning, and scan metadata. This run returned route=graph, reason=verified_tag_context_selected, facet coverage 81.51%, context_bytes=3174, 6 hits, 21 evidence pointers, scan_complete=true, and fail_closed=false. Graph sufficiency requires verified spans plus all required facets and at least 60% weighted coverage; when proof obligations exist, every obligation must be covered. It defers for insufficient prompt facets, custody mismatch, unauthenticated matches, no tag match, missing required coverage, missing spans, sensitive-path exclusion, or capped/incomplete scans. Sensitive-path and incomplete-scan overrides occur in the adapter after core retrieval. Empty usable source or invalid input exits with an error instead of returning a routing result.
